samples.summary: "a paste clears it" and "insertImage clears it" pass whether or not the image selection is cleared
samples.evidence: Both tests assert only `expect(editor.getSelectedImage()).toBeNull()` after a mutation that INSERTS text ahead of the selected offset. `getSelectedImage()` (editor.ts:3742-3753) re-validates via `findImageAtOffset(block, offset)` and returns null whenever the offset no longer holds an image. In the paste test the block becomes `XYZab￼c￼d`, so offset 2 is the character `Z`; in the insertImage test an image is inserted at offset 0, so offset 2 is `b`. In both cases `getSelectedImage()` returns null even if `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` were never called — the assertion cannot fail. The file's own `blockWithTwoImages` helper documents the only way to make a stale selection observable (a mutation that slides IMAGE2 *onto* offset 2, i.e. a deletion), and the cut test does exactly that, but these two do not. So the `applyPastePlan` clearer hook and the `insertImage` clear (the paths whose failure lets a stale selection name the wrong image and lets the next Delete remove it) are effectively uncovered. (The sibling `insertTable clears it` test is fine: the cursor is at offset 0 so `b1` is not split and offset 2 still holds IMAGE.)

samples.summary: No test covers the new `!readOnly` guard on the image resize-drag branch
samples.evidence: The diff removes the blanket `if (readOnly) return;` from `handleImageMouseDown` and replaces it with a narrower `if (!readOnly && selectedImage)` on the handle-hit branch. That guard is now the only thing stopping a viewer from starting a resize drag: `handleImageResizeMouseUp` (editor.ts:2488-2524) has no read-only check of its own and calls `docStore.snapshot()` + `doc.applyInlineStyle`, and the api-level `MUTATING_METHODS` noop list (editor.ts:3903) does not cover this DOM path. Nothing in the new test file, `packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts`, or anywhere in packages/docs/test dispatches a mousedown on an image handle at all — the only read-only mousedown test ("a click elsewhere clears a read-only image selection") deliberately misses every image at 0,0. If the `!readOnly` were dropped, a read-only document would be silently mutated and every suite would stay green.
searchedFor: grep readOnly in packages/docs/test (2 files: editor-read-only.test.ts, copy-integrity.test.ts)

samples.summary: The read-only → `handles: false` wiring (editor → DocCanvas → drawImageSelection) is untested; only the leaf function is
samples.evidence: `image-selection-overlay.test.ts` adds a test calling `drawImageSelection(ctx, rect, { handles: false })` directly, which proves the option works but not that anything ever passes it. Nothing constructs `new DocCanvas(canvas, true)` or asserts that a read-only `initialize(...)` results in a handle-less overlay — grep for `new DocCanvas` in packages/docs/test returns no matches. A regression that drops the `readOnly` argument in editor.ts:951 or the `{ handles: !this.readOnly }` in doc-canvas.ts would leave both suites green while viewers see eight non-functional resize handles.

samples.summary: `applySpellSuggestion` and `insertPageNumber` gain `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` calls with no test
samples.evidence: The diff adds the clear to four programmatic mutation entry points; the new test file covers only paste, insertTable and insertImage (`describe('mutations that shift the offsets under an image selection')`), and two of those three are vacuous (see the separate finding). No test in packages/docs/test calls `applySpellSuggestion` or `insertPageNumber` with an image selection live, so those two clears could be deleted without any suite noticing. Same failure mode as the others: a stale (blockId, offset) selection naming a different inline after offsets shift.
searchedFor: grep applySpellSuggestion / insertPageNumber usage in packages/docs/test
read the 'mutations that shift the offsets' describe block in copy-integrity.test.ts

samples.summary: No test that a mousedown on an image BODY selects it in read-only — the headline new viewer capability
samples.evidence: Every read-only image test reaches the selection through the programmatic `editor.selectImageAt(...)`, not through the mouse path the change enables. The one mousedown test ("a click elsewhere clears a read-only image selection") deliberately clicks at 0,0 where no image is, exercising branch 3 only. Branch 2 (`findImageAtPoint` hit → `selectImageInline`) in read-only — the path a real viewer uses before Cmd+C — has no coverage. It shares code with the editable path, which is why this is contained rather than major.

samples.summary: The null-`clipboardData` early return is only tested with an image selection, not with a text selection
samples.evidence: `handleCopy`/`handleCut` were restructured so `const clipboard = e.clipboardData; if (!clipboard) return;` runs before `preventDefault()` for ALL paths, including the ordinary text-selection copy/cut. The new tests ("a null clipboardData leaves the copy to the browser", "a null clipboardData cuts nothing at all") both set up an image selection and no text selection, so they exit through the image branch. No test dispatches a null-clipboardData copy/cut with a text selection live, which is the far more common case and the one where an unguarded cut would delete content that reached no clipboard.

samples.summary: The new `render()` in the imageKeyHandler catch-all is not asserted
samples.evidence: The diff adds `render()` next to `selectedImage = null` in the catch-all branch specifically so the overlay is repainted for keys TextEditor ignores. The corresponding test ("a non-modifier key still drops the image selection", F5) asserts only `getSelectedImage()` is null; it would pass with the `render()` removed, leaving the stale overlay painted. No render/paint spy exists in this suite.

samples.summary: Test (e) asserts only that a mock was called
samples.evidence: `expect(copy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` with `editor.copy` fully mocked — the real `editor.copy()` (focus + execCommand) is mocked away, so the test proves menu wiring only. That is acceptable for a menu component and the docs-side read-only copy is covered by `editor-read-only.test.ts:229`, so this is a style point rather than a coverage hole; noting it for completeness. The test also does not assert the menu closes after the click.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. `getSelectedImage()` (editor.ts:3742-3753) re-validates via `findImageAtOffset` (model/types.ts:457-467), which returns null unless the stored offset falls inside an image inline. In 'a paste clears it' (copy-integrity.test.ts:1017-1039) the block becomes `XYZab￼c￼d`, so stored offset 2 is the character `Z`; in 'insertImage clears it' (1051-1065) an image is inserted at offset 0 so offset 2 is `b`. In both cases `getSelectedImage()` returns null regardless of whether the selection was cleared, so the sole assertion cannot fail — the applyPastePlan clearer hook and the `clearImageSelectionForMutation()` call in `insertImage` (editor.ts:3716) are effectively uncovered. The discriminating technique exists in the same file (the cut test at 844-876 slides IMAGE2 onto offset 2 and asserts the follow-up Delete), and a repo-wide grep shows `getSelectedImage`/`applyPastePlan`/`imageSelectionClearer` appear in no other test file, so no alternative coverage exists. Vacuous coverage for a change whose failure lets a stale selection name the wrong image and lets the next Delete remove it: major under the test-adequacy rubric.

verdict.reason: Verified the guard and searched wide for any covering test; none exists. editor.ts:2559 (`if (!readOnly && selectedImage)`) is the sole read-only stopper for the DOM resize-drag path: handleImageResizeMouseUp (editor.ts:2488-2524) commits via docStore.snapshot() + doc.applyInlineStyle at 2512-2520 with no read-only check, and the MUTATING_METHODS noop list (editor.ts:3903-3914) patches only API methods, not this DOM path. For tests: only three files in packages/docs reference MouseEvent/mousedown (editor-contextmenu.test.ts — no image/readOnly usage; cell-hf-wrap-affinity.test.ts — not read-only; copy-integrity.test.ts). The single read-only mousedown test, copy-integrity.test.ts:988-1008, dispatches at 0,0 and asserts getSelectedImage() becomes null, proving it lands in the "click elsewhere" branch (editor.ts:2598-2604), so it stays green with or without `!readOnly`. editor-read-only.test.ts has zero occurrences of "image" and no MouseEvent. Repo-wide, selectImageAt/getSelectedImage/updateSelectedImage appear only in copy-integrity.test.ts and editor.ts; image-selection-overlay.test.ts covers only pure helpers with no editor instance; there is no e2e/playwright suite and no test references imageResizeDrag. Missing test for a changed behavior whose failure silently weakens a read-only guard and mutates a viewer's document — in-lane and major.
